name: Helping Hands (application and ID help)
description: Helping Hands assists with Medi-Cal, CalFresh, and General Assistance applications and ID cards.
notes: Guide gives no address or hours.

name: IRS Free File / VITA Tax Clinics
description: Free tax preparation for low-income and homeless individuals, including patients without a fixed address; can help access the Earned Income Tax Credit and stimulus/rebate programs. Various community sites countywide (seasonal).

name: Medi-Cal, CalFresh, and cash aid (San Mateo County Human Services)
description: San Mateo County Human Services office in East Palo Alto. Medi-Cal (health coverage), CalFresh (food benefits), and General Assistance (cash aid).
hours: Mon to Fri, 8 am to 5 pm

name: Medi-Cal, CalFresh, and cash aid (Santa Clara County Social Services)
description: Santa Clara County Social Services handles Medi-Cal (health coverage), CalFresh (food benefits), and General Assistance (cash aid).
notes: Milpitas guide: Hope for the Unhoused volunteers assist with applications. Sunnyvale guide: Helping Hands assists with applications and ID cards (408-663-1812).

name: SOAR (SSI/SSDI Outreach, Access, and Recovery)
description: Specialized technical assistance model to speed up SSI/SSDI approvals for people experiencing homelessness with a disabling condition. Ask the case manager whether a county SOAR-trained worker is available.
eligibility: People experiencing homelessness with a disabling condition

name: Social Security Administration (SSI/SSDI)
description: SSI/SSDI applications for patients with qualifying disabilities, benefit verification letters, and replacement Social Security cards. Homeless status can be used for mail/payment routing via representative payee or agency address.
notes: Guide says to verify local office hours before visiting.

name: St. Anthony's (free clothing)
description: Distributes clothing weekly: Wednesdays 10 to 11 am (women and children) and Thursdays (men).
hours: Wednesdays 10 to 11 am (women and children); Thursdays (men)

name: St. Vincent de Paul Society - Santa Clara County Council
description: Free clothing, furniture, household goods, and basic necessities via home visits and parish conferences. Contact the nearest parish conference (varies by ZIP).

name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Line
description: Suicide and mental health crisis line. Call or text, any time. Spanish available.
hours: Any time
notes: 'Spanish available' is stated in the Mountain View and San Jose guides.

name: Behavioral Health Urgent Care (BHUC)
description: Walk-in crisis clinic for people uninsured or on Medi-Cal: screening, crisis intervention, short-term treatment, medication refills. Open every day.
hours: Every day, 8 am to 7 pm

name: Momentum Crisis Stabilization Unit
description: Voluntary alternative to the ER for adults 18 and over in a mental health crisis who do not need medical detox. Up to 24 hours with meals, showers, and clinical support. TRUST can provide transport.
address: 101 Jose Figueres Ave, Suite 50, San Jose
hours: Walk in, 24 hours
eligibility: Adults 18+ in a mental health crisis who do not need medical detox

name: StarVista crisis line
description: San Mateo County crisis line. 24-hour crisis counseling. Mobile crisis team available.
hours: 24 hours (any time)

name: TRUST mobile crisis team
description: Mobile crisis team, 24 hours, comes to you. Spanish available. TRUST can provide transport to the Momentum Crisis Stabilization Unit.
hours: 24 hours

name: Veterans Crisis Line
description: For veterans in crisis or their loved ones. Call 988 then press 1, or text 838255.
eligibility: Veterans in crisis or their loved ones

name: Foothill College Dental Hygiene Clinic
description: Low-cost cleanings by supervised students; appointments are limited.
address: 12345 El Monte Rd, Los Altos Hills
hours: Mon, Wed, Thu 9 to 12; Tue 1:30 to 4:30

name: CORA domestic violence hotline
description: 24-hour domestic violence hotline and confidential shelter.
hours: Any time

name: Next Door Solutions to Domestic Violence
description: DV shelter, counseling, and legal advocacy program.
hours: 24-hour hotline

name: YWCA 24-hour line
description: 24-hour line for domestic violence, sexual assault, or trafficking.
hours: Any time

name: 911 Emergency
description: Police, fire, or medical. Ask for a mental health crisis clinician or CIT officer. For a medical emergency, call 911.
notes: Mountain View and San Jose guides say to ask for a mental health crisis clinician or CIT officer; Milpitas, East Palo Alto, and Sunnyvale guides say 'Police, fire, or medical'.

name: El Camino Health (emergency room)
description: Emergency room. For a medical emergency, call 911.

name: Poison Control
description: Suspected poisoning or overdose information.

name: Regional Medical Center (emergency room)
description: Emergency room. For a medical emergency, call 911.

name: Stanford Hospital (emergency room)
description: Emergency room. For a medical emergency, call 911.

name: Valley Medical Center (emergency room)
description: Emergency room. For a medical emergency, call 911.

name: CalFresh Employment & Training (CFET)
description: Free, voluntary job skills and training program for CalFresh recipients. Via SSA.

name: Goodwill Silicon Valley (job training)
description: Job training, veteran employment services, and supportive employment programs.

name: HomeFirst Employment Training
description: Employment placement and self-sufficiency workshops integrated with shelter case management.
notes: 408-510-7600 is the HomeFirst helpline; the guide lists it for several HomeFirst programs.

name: NOVA Workforce Board / America's Job Center of California
description: Free job search assistance, resume help, training referrals, and unemployment insurance navigation.
address: 196 N. 3rd St., San Jose (and other sites)

name: CalFresh Food (SNAP) - Santa Clara County SSA
description: Monthly EBT food benefit. Apply online, by phone, or in person; document drop boxes at SSA offices. Expedited service (benefits within 3 days) for very low-income households. Homeless, elderly, and disabled clients may use EBT for hot prepared meals at participating restaurants (Restaurant Meals Program).

name: CSA food pantry
description: Groceries for Mountain View residents through Community Services Agency.
hours: Mon and Fri 2 to 4 pm; Thu 11:30 am to 1 pm

name: Ecumenical Hunger Program (EHP)
description: Food boxes, no-cook food bags for people without a kitchen, hot lunch, clothing (clothes closet), blankets, and household items.
hours: Food pickup Mon to Thu, 9 am to 12 pm and 2 to 5 pm; hot lunch Mon to Thu, 12 to 1 pm

name: Hope's Corner
description: Free hot breakfast and bag lunch. Free showers and laundry for unhoused guests; sign-up during the meal, first come, first served. Restrooms with hand-washing open 24 hours.
hours: Meals: Mon and Wed 8 to 9 am; Sat 8 to 10 am. Showers and laundry: Mon and Wed 8:30 am to 12 pm; Sat 8:30 am to 2 pm. Restrooms: 24 hours
eligibility: Showers and laundry for unhoused guests

name: Loaves & Fishes free meals (Goodwill, San Jose)
description: Free prepared meals.
hours: Mondays 3 to 4 pm

name: Loaves & Fishes free meals (Jerry Larson FoodBasket)
description: Free prepared meals.
hours: Fridays 1 to 2 pm

name: Loaves & Fishes free meals (Los Robles / McNair Academy)
description: Free prepared meals, packed to go.
address: Los Robles / McNair Academy, 2033 Pulgas Ave, East Palo Alto
hours: Mondays, 2 to 3 pm

name: Loaves & Fishes free meals (Mountain View High School)
description: Free prepared meals, packed to go.
address: Mountain View High School, 3535 Truman Ave
hours: Thursdays, 3:30 to 4:30 pm

name: Loaves & Fishes free meals (Piedmont Hills High School)
description: Free prepared hot meal.
address: Piedmont Hills High School, 1377 Piedmont Rd, San Jose
hours: Mon to Fri 4 to 5 pm (hot meal)

name: Loaves & Fishes free meals (San Miguel Elementary)
description: Free prepared meals, packed to go.
address: San Miguel Elementary, 777 San Miguel Ave, Sunnyvale
hours: Tuesdays, 3:30 to 4:30 pm

name: Loaves & Fishes free meals (Weller Elementary, Milpitas)
description: Free prepared meals.
hours: Mondays 3:30 to 4:30 pm
notes: Milpitas site closes for summer break through August 30, 2026.

name: Martha's Kitchen
description: Free hot meals served daily to anyone in need, no ID or eligibility screening required.
eligibility: Anyone in need; no ID or eligibility screening

name: Milpitas Food Pantry
description: Free groceries for residents of Milpitas and Alviso. Photo ID and proof of residence requested.
hours: Tue, Thu, Sat, 9 am to 12 pm
eligibility: Residents of Milpitas and Alviso; photo ID and proof of residence requested

name: Our Daily Bread
description: Free hot lunch and grocery bags, open to anyone. Across from Washington Park, near the library.
address: St. Thomas Episcopal Church, 231 Sunset Ave
hours: Mon, Wed, Fri, 11 am to 12:30 pm

name: Reaching Out Center
description: Food and basic necessities.
hours: Mon to Fri 9 am to 5 pm
notes: Guide gives no address.

name: Sacred Heart Community Service
description: Food pantry with no-cook bags for people without a kitchen, plus a clothes closet.
hours: Mon to Thu 9 am to 4 pm

values.value: 408-283-6114 (Food Pantry)
408-916-5053 (Clothes Closet)

name: Second Harvest Food Connection
description: Lists free grocery and hot meal sites by ZIP code. English, Spanish, Vietnamese, Chinese, Tagalog.
hours: Mon to Fri, 8 am to 5 pm (phone)
notes: Text GETFOOD to 408-455-5181. The East Palo Alto guide lists only the 800 number.

name: Senior Nutrition Program
description: Congregate and home-delivered meals for adults 60+ at 35+ meal sites countywide, including Meals on Wheels for homebound seniors. Via SSA.

name: USDA SNAP (CalFresh) Federal Info Line
description: General SNAP/CalFresh program information. Local applications go through Santa Clara County SSA.

name: WeHOPE Family Harvest
description: Free boxes of groceries with fresh food, with Second Harvest.
hours: Every Tuesday, 11:30 am to 1 pm

name: WIC (Women, Infants & Children)
description: Federal nutrition program for pregnant and postpartum people and children under 5. Santa Clara County Public Health Dept.

name: California Housing Is Key (housing.ca.gov)
description: State clearinghouse for tenant protections, eviction help, and rental assistance program information.

name: CalWORKs Housing Support Program (HSP)
description: State-funded rapid rehousing and housing stabilization for CalWORKs-eligible families. Apply through Santa Clara County Social Services Agency (SSA).

name: Community Services Agency (CSA)
description: Homeless case management, housing search help, benefits and transit help, and one-time financial assistance. Restrooms with hand-washing open 24 hours.
hours: Mon to Fri 9 am to 4 pm
notes: Office hours Mon to Fri 9 am to 4 pm; restrooms open 24 hours (per the Mountain View guide's showers section).

name: County Office of Supportive Housing
description: Santa Clara County Office of Supportive Housing runs the housing programs.

name: Goodwill Silicon Valley - Veterans Programs
description: SSVF partner agency offering veteran-specific rapid rehousing and employment services.

name: HomeFirst Housing Opportunities for Everyone (HOPE) / Rapid Rehousing
description: Flexible one-time assistance (deposits, application fees, moving costs) plus short-term rental subsidy and housing navigation case management.
notes: 408-510-7600 is the HomeFirst helpline; the guide lists it for several HomeFirst programs.

name: Homelessness Prevention line
description: Covers rent assistance and legal support for people at risk of losing housing.
eligibility: People at risk of losing housing

values.value: Homelessness Prevention line: rent assistance and legal support for people at risk of losing housing.
values.source: Hope's Corner (Mountain View); Hope for the Unhoused (Milpitas); Neighborhood Hands (San Jose); Helping Hands (Sunnyvale Library)

values.value: Homelessness Prevention System (HPS): one-time or short-term financial assistance (rent, deposit, utilities), legal support, and case management for households at risk of losing housing. No longer restricted by ZIP code.

Family Shelter Waiting List Hotline (same number, 408-926-8885): families with children must call daily 10 to 11 am to remain on the shared shelter waiting list. Also given as the access line for the HomeFirst Family Shelters.

notes: Mountain View and San Jose guides mention rent assistance only; Milpitas and Sunnyvale guides add legal support and the website.

name: Housing Authority of the County of Santa Clara (HACSC)
description: Administers Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers, public housing, and HUD-VASH rental vouchers for veterans (in partnership with the VA; over 1,200 vouchers allocated to the county). Waitlists may be closed periodically; check status before referring.
address: 505 W. Julian St., San Jose, CA 95110

name: Milpitas outreach team
description: The City of Milpitas partners with WeHOPE for street outreach, housing assessments, and case management in Milpitas. Email: housing@milpitas.gov.

name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans (VA)
description: First call for any homeless or at-risk veteran. Connects veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness to the nearest VA homeless programs (SSVF, HUD-VASH, Grant Per Diem, and healthcare enrollment).
eligibility: Veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness

name: Sunnyvale Community Services
description: Emergency rent and utility assistance, case workers, referrals, and food for Sunnyvale residents. Food program: weekly groceries for enrolled Sunnyvale households, plus a pantry for unhoused community members. Enrollment at the front desk or by phone.
hours: Office: Mon to Fri, 9 to 12 and 12:30 to 4. Food program: Wednesdays, 9 am to 6 pm
eligibility: Sunnyvale residents; food pantry also open to unhoused community members

name: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) - HomeFirst
description: Rapid rehousing and homelessness prevention case management and financial assistance for veteran households. First-come shelter check-in at 3:30 pm before VA bed eligibility screening.
address: 2011 Little Orchard Blvd., San Jose, CA

name: VA Palo Alto Health Care System (HUD-VASH)
description: HUD-VASH voucher program (rental vouchers combined with VA case management for eligible homeless veterans, administered with HACSC), VA health enrollment, and homeless veteran case management.

name: Veterans Resource Centers of America
description: SSVF partner offering case management and housing assistance for veterans.
notes: Guide gives no phone or address; it says to check the current listing via 211.

name: WeHOPE outreach in Sunnyvale
description: City-contracted outreach workers for housing assessments, housing resources, and health services.
hours: Mon to Fri, 9 am to 1 pm (650-629-4290); Sat and Sun, 9 am to 1 pm (650-942-1926)

name: Asian Law Alliance
description: Multilingual civil legal aid. Walk-in and phone general consultations weekday mornings; immigration clinic by appointment (Fridays and Saturdays).
address: 991 W. Hedding St., Suite 202, San Jose, CA 95126
hours: General consultations Mon to Fri mornings (walk in or phone); immigration clinic by appointment, Fridays and Saturdays

name: Bay Area Legal Aid
description: Free civil legal help for low-income residents: housing/eviction, domestic violence, public benefits denials, and family law. San Jose office, serves Santa Clara County.

name: CARAS (Community Agency for Resources, Advocacy & Services)
description: Legal and eviction assistance for South County residents.
eligibility: South County residents only (Gilroy, San Martin, Morgan Hill)
notes: Guide gives no phone or address; it says to call 211 for current contact information.

name: Catholic Charities of Santa Clara County - Immigration & Legal Services
description: DOJ-recognized agency; accredited representatives assist with citizenship, DACA, family petitions, and general immigration counseling.
address: 2625 Zanker Rd., Suite 201, San Jose, CA 95134

name: City of San Jose Eviction Help Center
description: Explains the eviction process and connects tenants to legal and financial resources (does not give legal advice directly). Email: evictionhelp@sanjoseca.gov.

name: Katharine & George Alexander Community Law Center (Santa Clara University School of Law)
description: Free clinic covering consumer, employment, and immigration law for low-income residents.

name: Law Foundation of Silicon Valley
description: Housing Program: free eviction defense, fair-housing/discrimination claims, Section 8/Housing Authority hearings, and HPS legal support. Also runs the Mental Health Advocacy Project and Health Legal Services for clients of the Valley Homeless Healthcare Program. Does not specialize in immigration law but can advise on how immigration status affects public benefits.
address: 4 North Second St., San Jose, CA 95113

values.value: 408-280-2424 (Housing Program intake, Legal Aid section)
408-280-2420 (Immigration Services section)

notes: The guide gives two numbers that differ by one digit in different sections. Verify which is current.

name: National Immigration Legal Services Directory
description: Searchable directory of vetted nonprofit immigration legal providers; useful to confirm an agency is still active before referring. Only a licensed attorney or a BIA-accredited representative may legally give immigration advice or file petitions; unauthorized 'notario' services are a common source of fraud.

name: Office of Immigrant Relations (OIR) - County of Santa Clara
description: County office (Division of Equity & Social Justice) coordinating funded immigration legal partners (VAWA/U-Visa/T-Visa, DACA, citizenship, removal defense). Good starting point for referrals and the current partner list.

name: Pro Bono Project Silicon Valley
description: Civil legal aid via volunteer attorneys: consumer, employment, and family law referrals.
address: 25 N. 14th St., Suite 506, San Jose, CA 95112

name: Project Sentinel
description: Free counseling on eviction notices, tenant/landlord rights, and fair housing complaints. Serves Santa Clara County.

name: Santa Clara County Superior Court Self-Help Center
description: In-person help with court forms; emergency same-day filing assistance for unlawful detainer (eviction) Answers.
address: Family Justice Center, 201 N. First St., 1st Floor, San Jose
hours: Mon to Thu, 8:30 am to 1:30 pm; Fri, 8:30 am to noon

name: SIREN (Services, Immigrant Rights & Education Network)
description: Rapid-response support for immigrants in crisis (24/7), know-your-rights workshops, community navigator training, and legal service referrals.
address: 1415 Koll Circle, Suite 108, San Jose, CA 95112
hours: Rapid-response support 24/7

name: USCIS Contact Center
description: Official immigration case status, forms, and application information. Will not give legal advice.

name: Gardner / CompreCare Health Center
description: Medical and dental care in English, Spanish, and Vietnamese. Psychiatric care (by referral), housing, and case management. Call first.
hours: Mon to Fri 8 am to 5 pm; Saturday dental
notes: Psychiatric care is by referral.

name: MayView Community Health Center
description: Primary care and behavioral health on a sliding scale ($10 to $40 if uninsured), many languages. Second site: 270 Grant Ave, Palo Alto. Call first.
hours: Mon and Fri 8 to 5; Tue to Thu 8 am to 7 pm; 2nd and 4th Sat 9 to 4

name: North County Mobile Health Center (Valley Homeless Healthcare Program)
description: Free medical care, psychiatry, and social work for people experiencing homelessness in Santa Clara County. The mobile clinic visits Hope's Corner in Mountain View on the days listed. First come, first served. A street medicine team can also be requested by referral.
address: Hope's Corner, 748 Mercy St, Mountain View
hours: 2nd Wed 8:30 to 11:30 am; 1st Thu 9:30 am to 12 pm; 2nd and 4th Thu 9:30 am to 4 pm

name: North County Mobile Health Center (Valley Homeless Healthcare Program) - Sunnyvale HomeFirst Shelter
description: Mobile clinic with outreach specialists, psychiatrists, psychologists, physicians, and social workers. Access via the Valley Homeless Healthcare Program.
hours: Mondays and Thursdays
notes: Guide gives no phone for this stop ('Via VHHP') and no street address. The same mobile clinic's Hope's Corner stop is a separate entry.

name: Peninsula Healthcare Connection
description: Free clinic for people experiencing homelessness. Insurance not required. Medical care, counseling, psychiatric medication, substance use treatment.

name: Ravenswood Family Health Network
description: Community clinic near WeHOPE. Primary care, dental, eye care, counseling, pharmacy. Serves patients regardless of insurance or immigration status. Sliding scale fees ($20 to $50); accepts Medi-Cal. Call first.
hours: Mon to Thu 8 am to 7 pm (Tue from 9:30); Fri 8 to 5; Sat 8 to 1

name: Destination: Home
description: Countywide backbone organization coordinating housing funds, landlord engagement, and systems-level rehousing initiatives, including the All the Way Home veterans campaign (coordination of veteran housing resources and landlord recruitment).

name: HUD Exchange / Continuum of Care (CoC) Programs
description: Federal funding source and policy for Continuum of Care, HMIS, and homeless-assistance programs. Administered locally by OSH as CoC Lead; general public inquiries go through local OSH/CoC partners rather than HUD directly.

name: MyConnectSV
description: Patient-facing HMIS portal that lets clients view their own record and securely message their care team. Ask OSH or a case manager for portal access.

name: Pet food: Humane Society Pet Pantry
description: Free pet food for county residents with financial need, while supplies last.

name: California Department of Public Health - Vital Records
description: Replacement birth certificates. State office (Sacramento) or the County Recorder's Office locally. A no-fee or reduced-fee process may be available for homeless applicants through some County Recorder offices; verify current local policy.

name: California DMV - Fee Waiver / Homeless ID
description: Fee waiver available for a state ID card for people experiencing homelessness. An agency or shelter can provide a homeless-verification letter in place of standard proof of residency. Local DMV field offices.

name: The United Effort Organization (at Hope's Corner)
description: Help with IDs, phones, public benefits, and housing navigation, on site during meals.
address: Hope's Corner, 748 Mercy St, Mountain View
hours: Wed 8 to 9 am; Sat 8:30 to 10:30 am

name: Milpitas Library
description: Restrooms, water, free Wi-Fi, computers, phone charging.
hours: Open every day from 10 am (closes 7 pm; 9 pm Mon to Thu)

name: Sunnyvale Public Library
description: Restrooms, water, free Wi-Fi, computers, phone charging.
hours: Mon to Thu 10 am to 9 pm; Fri and Sat 10 to 6; Sun 1 to 6

name: Amigos de Guadalupe safe parking
description: Overnight parking with case management.
notes: Guide gives no address or hours.

name: Move Mountain View safe parking
description: For people living in a car or RV. Move Mountain View operates staffed overnight safe parking lots with restrooms.
notes: Guides do not list lot addresses.

name: WeHOPE safe parking
description: For people living in a car or RV. WeHOPE operates a safe parking program. Information through WeHOPE or 211.
notes: Guide gives no lot address.

name: Cold Weather Shelter Program
description: Seasonal overnight shelter opened during cold or wet weather at rotating sites countywide; operated in partnership with HomeFirst and OSH. Call Here4You (408-385-2400) or 408-278-6420.

name: Here4You Hotline
description: Referrals to emergency shelters and housing waitlists in Santa Clara County.
hours: 9 am to 7 pm, every day

name: HomeFirst Boccardo Reception Center (BRC)
description: Largest shelter in the county. Congregate shelter for single adults not accompanied by minor children. On-site medical clinic, showers, laundry, meals, case management, and employment services. Showers, laundry, and hygiene kits for shelter guests and outreach clients. Bus Line 26.
eligibility: Single adults not accompanied by minor children
notes: 408-510-7600 is the HomeFirst helpline; the guide lists it for several HomeFirst programs.

name: HomeFirst Emergency Interim Housing (Tiny Homes)
